text: From m1's ACCEPT cross-review of the landed W3 correction a15396e (post-01M15PTM9JGBTRA8560M5FZKEM). Two follow-ups, both accepted by the chief. NIT 1 (defense in depth, the one that matters): PseudonymizationDetector.validateTransformation is private[embed] and its positional zip is correct ONLY because its single caller, PseudonymizedText.checked, first asserts sourceDetection.spans == offsets.map(_._1). A future embed-core caller could pass offsets in another order and get pairwise comparisons against the wrong table entries. Fix: inside the zip, also require matched.span == the offset's source span, failing with the same typed InvariantViolation. That makes the invariant local instead of caller-dependent. NIT 2 (documentation): under caseInsensitive, Turkish dotted capital I (U+0130) folds onto ASCII i, so a row 'ismail' detects 'ISMAIL' spelled with U+0130. The direction is fail-safe - over-detection means more redaction and destination re-detection only gets stricter - but detector identity is supposed to FIX behaviour, so the folding rule needs a sentence in the Scaladoc beside the whole-word rule. Scope: privacy.scala + PrivacySuite only. Rebase onto 6a4a7c0. Owner: codex-storymodel-new-engineer (volunteered).
